[FACT] User is concerned about the impact of social media on teenagers' mental health.  
[PREFERENCE] User believes social media companies should be held accountable for the negative impact their platforms have on teenagers' mental health.  
[PREFERENCE] User thinks social media platforms should do more to prevent harmful content from being shared.  
[PREFERENCE] User feels it is unfair that social media companies profit off the negative impact their platforms have on teenagers' mental health.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The rise of social media has affected teenagers' mental health in both positive and negative ways, connecting them with like-minded individuals while also being associated with depression, anxiety, and body image issues.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Social media creates pressure for teenagers to present themselves in a particular way, leading to comparison and self-criticism.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Exposure to cyberbullying and online hate can contribute to negative mental health outcomes for teenagers.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Parents and educators can promote a healthy relationship with social media by setting limits on screen time, monitoring use, and encouraging offline activities.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Social media companies have a responsibility to regulate harmful content, but parents and educators also play an important role in protecting young users.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Social media companies have algorithms to flag harmful content, but these systems are not always foolproof.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Protecting young users from harmful material is a joint effort between social media companies, parents, and educators.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Social media companies should continue to invest in research into the impact of their platforms on mental health and develop innovative solutions to mitigate potential negative effects.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Social media companies should ensure their moderation policies and algorithms are effective in identifying and removing harmful content.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Social media companies should provide resources to support users struggling with mental health issues.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Social media companies should develop and refine policies and technology to detect and remove potentially harmful content.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Social media companies could invest in AI-based systems to proactively identify and remove harmful content.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Social media companies should offer users access to mental health support and education about mental health.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] There are regulations in many countries requiring social media companies to remove harmful content and protect user privacy.
